Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design.

This review examines targeted protein degradation as a therapeutic strategy, focusing on PROTACs that hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate disease-causing proteins rather than merely inhibiting them. It discusses key determinants of successful PROTAC translation—including target degradability and E3 ligase recruitment—and how AI-driven design is being integrated into the field. The paper synthesizes ubiquitination biology with drug discovery approaches to guide future development.

canSAR 2026-an update to the public drug discovery knowledgebase.

canSAR 2026 is an updated release of the world's largest public knowledgebase for cancer drug discovery and translational research. It integrates multidisciplinary public and curated data into a connected knowledge map and adds enhanced machine learning and AI tools for generating novel drug discovery insights. The update highlights growth across all data types and improvements to predictive algorithms.

DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome.

DGIdb 2026 is an updated open-access knowledgebase that aggregates and normalizes drug-gene interaction data from many sources, now adding three new datasets (Molecular Oncology Almanac, PRISM Repurposing, and Broad Institute Drug Repurposing). The release also improves programmatic access and local deployment options, making it easier for researchers to integrate druggable-genome data into their own pipelines.

Artificial intelligence in basic and translational cardiovascular research.

This narrative review surveys how machine learning and deep learning are being applied across cardiovascular research, from medical imaging and computational omics to mechanistic simulation and drug discovery. It emphasizes the need to distinguish genuine AI contributions from routine bioinformatics and purely biophysical modeling, and it evaluates studies based on independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference. The review is aimed at helping researchers judge the rigor and translational potential of AI-based cardiovascular studies.

Design, synthesis, and docking analysis of benzene sulfonamide-[1,4]benzoxazepine hybrids as acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors.

The authors synthesized a series of hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-sulfonamide compounds and tested them as inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), enzymes targeted in Alzheimer's disease therapy. Several compounds showed micromolar dual inhibition, with compound 12j being the most potent BChE inhibitor (IC50 = 1.06 µM) and compound 9d showing the greatest BChE selectivity. Docking analysis was used to rationalize binding interactions.

This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can drive both protective immunity and chronic inflammatory pathology. The authors integrate cheminformatics and machine-learning approaches to identify and prioritize potential TLR-targeted therapeutic compounds for Mycoplasma infections. The work bridges immunopathogenesis with computational drug-discovery strategies for these minimal-genome pathogens.

Synthesis and antiproliferative screening of para-halogenated 4H-chromene-benzene hybrids: crystallographic, and molecular-docking studies.

This paper reports a fast, high-yield synthesis of 4H-chromene-benzene hybrids with para-halogen substituents, using an ultrasonic-assisted one-pot reaction that completes in 2 minutes with 93-96% yield. The compounds were structurally characterized, including by X-ray crystallography, and screened for antiproliferative activity against twelve human cancer cell lines. The 4-chloro derivative (4b) showed the broadest activity, with molecular docking used to explore possible binding interactions.

BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.

The paper introduces BioLM-Score, a protein-ligand scoring method that conditions geometric probabilistic potentials on pretrained biomolecular language model representations. The authors test whether these language-model priors improve scoring performance over a controlled geometric baseline across affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening tasks. The work probes whether pretrained representations can mitigate poor generalization of geometric likelihood models when structural training coverage is limited.

Drug Repurposing in Pre-Eclampsia: Maternal Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Considerations for Clinical Trial Design.

Democratizing Drug Discovery: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Massive Specific Protein Target QSAR Modeling Using ChEMBL.
